newsitem.title: USA: Rubin, Mitsuzuka share concern on recent yen moves.
newsitem.headline: Rubin, Mitsuzuka share concern on recent yen moves.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka voiced concern Sunday about recent movements of the Japanese yen on world currency markets, a U.S. Treasury spokeswoman said.
The two men met ahead of a gathering of the Group of Seven industrial nations.
"Minister Mitsuzuka expressed concern about recent movements of the yen," the spokeswoman said, "Secretary Rubin said he shared that concern.
"The ministers reaffirmed their commitment to cooperate closely in foreign exchange markets as appropriate," she added.

According to the U.S. Treasury spokeswoman, Mitsuzuka reaffirmed the Japanese government objective of promoting strong domestic demand-led growth and avoiding a significant increase in its trade surplus.
Mitsuzuka also told Rubin about the Japanese government's action to tackle problem loans in the real-estate market.
Mitsuzuka expressed his desire for a continuation of the recent economic performance of the United States with low inflation.
"Minister Mitsuzuka expressed hope that the recent economic performance of the United States, with low inflation, would be sustained," the spokeswoman added.
For his part, Rubin welcomed Japan's commitment to economic deregulation and the steps it had taken to promote financial reform and strengthen its banking system, she said.
"Minister Mitsuzuka and Secretary Rubin reaffirmed the importance of maintaining a strong, cooperative relationship on economic and financial issues," the spokeswoman added.
A Japanese official later read the same statement to reporters.
